clue.text: Bend hard part of foot

parts.note: a bend or curve is an arc
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An instruction to flex the tough sole of your foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend' looks like the definition, but it supplies ARC; the definition is the part of the foot at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised curve on the underside of the foot is named for its bridge-like shape.

clue.text: Rising name in leaderless authoritarian system brings austere lifestyle

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the trimmed system
without its leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: fascism is an authoritarian political system

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A rising star within a beheaded dictatorship leads a spartan existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the first letter (ASCISM), and 'Rising' turns the naming word upwards (ETIC); in a down clue rising means reading bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Asceticism is the practice of severe self-denial, a lifestyle of austerity.

clue.text: Rover's whiskers mentioned in Hackney?

definitions.note: Rover is, with the 's standing for is; a rover is a pirate

indicators.note: spoken as a Cockney would say it, dropping the h; Hackney is a district of East London

parts.note: whiskers are coarse hair

explanation.surface: A dog named Rover has whiskers someone remarks on in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Cockney accent the h is dropped, so the phrase for whiskers comes out as 'coarse 'air'. HACKNEY is an East London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, and rover is an old word for a sea robber.

clue.text: Is small room covered by heaps of potpourri?

indicators.note: something covered by another piece sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

parts.note: heaps of something means many of it
taken as written
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: Asks whether a little room is buried under piles of dried scented petals.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection, which is exactly what a varied assortment of items is.

clue.text: It's not productive to make a deduction on old-fashioned hat

parts.note: to infer is to deduce
tile is dated slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Drawing conclusions about an antiquated hat gets you nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Infertile land or animals cannot produce offspring or crops, so they are unproductive.

clue.text: Gentlemen's leggings

definitions.meaning: fellows or blokes, informal for men

explanation.surface: Describing what well-bred men wear on their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps is informal for men, and also the name of cowboys' leather leg coverings.

clue.text: Firmly mould with a tongue-lashing?

parts.note: read literally, it suggests shaping something by licking it, as an animal grooms; the idiom means to discipline into proper form

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to bring into good order, which a severe scolding might do.

clue.text: City on Rhône river in which placard's top has come off

indicators.note: in which says the river holds the trimmed word

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

indicators.note: the top letter, in a down clue the first, is removed

parts.note: a placard is a sign

explanation.surface: A French town by the river where the head of a protest banner has fallen off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top has come off' leaves IGN, and 'in which' puts it inside the river. The Rhône is a major river of south-east France.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city on the river Rhône in southern France.

clue.text: French man aboard navy vessel

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French male first name.

clue.text: City of amusing character despite being loud

parts.note: a card is an old-fashioned word for a funny, eccentric person
if can mean even though, as in 'pleasant if dull'
F is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A town known for a comic figure who is noisy nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: CARDIFF is the capital city of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital is a city, so the plain word stands as a broad category definition.

clue.text: Ultimately, man in troubled City isn't evil, just following natural impulses

indicators.note: in says the single letter goes inside the rearranged phrase
troubled suggests disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word without its apostrophe

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of man is taken

explanation.surface: Ultimately a man in a disturbed city is not wicked, merely acting on instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges CITY ISNT EVIL, and 'in' puts N, the last letter of man, among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To act instinctively is to act purely on inborn impulse, without thought.

clue.text: I must wear funny braces for credit

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so the single letter goes inside the rearranged word
funny suggests something odd or out of place, so the letters of braces are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists they must put on comical trouser supports in exchange for credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges BRACES into ASCRBE, and 'must wear' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a work to someone is to attribute it to them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sinner's argot's disguised wrongdoing

indicators.note: something disguised has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word including its final S
the letters of the word including its final S

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer's slang hides the misdeed it describes.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the apostrophe-S of each word counts as a letter S: 'disguised' rearranges SINNERS and ARGOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A transgression is an act that breaks a rule or law, a direct synonym of a misdeed.

clue.text: Low body of water hides middle of downward path

indicators.note: the pool covers up the central letter, taking its place

parts.note: a descent is a downward path
a pond is a small body of water

explanation.surface: A pool lies in the middle of a sloping track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides middle of' replaces C, the central letter of DESCENT, with POND.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means feeling dejected, a common synonym of despondent.

clue.text: Love a duck, good one as pet in 9?

parts.note: 'Cor, love a duck!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise, so the phrase stands for the interjection cor
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Fondness for a waterbird, with a good one kept as a pet in the Welsh capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pembroke and Cardigan breeds are Welsh dogs, hence a pet in 9 (CARDIFF).
explanation.definitionFit: This small herding dog breed originated in Wales, so it is a pet you might find in the Welsh capital.

clue.text: One marks small change about to counter ineffectualness

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: about means going around, so the coins surround the reversed short word

parts.note: pence are small coins

indicators.note: counter means running in the opposite direction, so the word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A person keeping track of coins tallies them against powerlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' gives OT and 'about' wraps the coins round it. M for marks recalls the German currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotence means a lack of power or effectiveness, a synonym of ineffectualness.

clue.text: Enclosure on river ship broke

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
the Nile is the river of Egypt
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A fenced area beside a river and a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke means having no money at all.

clue.text: Newspaper to investigate summer holiday preparation

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
to screen people is to investigate or vet them

explanation.surface: A paper sets out to research what people pack for summer trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotion against sunburn is a typical item prepared for a summer beach trip.

clue.text: High point in Latin translation of wedding ceremony

indicators.note: to point one thing in is to direct it inside another
translation changes the form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: up means high, as in up in the air

explanation.surface: The peak moment in a Latin version of a marriage service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges the language name to give N, TIAL around the space, and 'point in' sets UP inside. 'High point' looks like one phrase, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding, used as an adjective here for the ceremony.

clue.text: Fix Kentish ram?

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Asks for a sheep from Kent to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix is a rigged arrangement or fraud, which is what a frame or set-up is.

clue.text: Things seem to vanish into this impression of slimness

definitions.text: Things seem to vanish into this

parts.note: thin describes slimness
an air is an impression or appearance, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A magician's place for making things disappear, or the look of being slender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two pieces: an air (impression) of being thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that vanish without trace are said to disappear into thin air, an idiom.

clue.text: Government sell-off placed one in hardship

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the longer word

parts.note: privation means hardship or want
the Roman numeral for one is I
sat can mean placed, as in sat the child on a chair

explanation.surface: A state asset sale has put someone in poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Privatisation is the transfer of a state-owned enterprise into private hands, a government sale.

clue.text: Behind time in arrangement of …

annotationWithheld.why: Behind time in arrangement of ... (5): the anagram fodder is the answer to 23 down (FEAR), reached through the ellipsis; no word of this clue gives those letters

clue.text: … Respect, following sense of music

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
an ear for music is a sense of it

explanation.surface: Deference coming after a feel for tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear can mean reverence or awe, as in fear of God.

clue.text: Demanding inclusion of Genesis in Exodus

indicators.note: inclusion of one thing in another means placing it inside, a container signal
in confirms the second piece holds the first

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure, an exit
Gen is the standard abbreviation for the book of Genesis

explanation.surface: Insisting the first book of the Bible be included in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding, as in exigent circumstances.

clue.text: Promote team though one short at breaks

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the team word is cut and the short word goes inside
one letter short means the final letter is taken off

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lift a side up the league even though it has a player missing at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one short' leaves ELEVE and 'breaks' splits it for AT. Football and cricket teams have eleven players, so a team is an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to raise them in rank, the same as promoting them.

clue.text: Improve bad-tempered off-road racing

parts.note: to rally is to recover or get better
cross means angry or bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Get better at grumpy cross-country motor sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a motor sport on mixed tarmac and dirt circuits, a form of racing partly off-road.

clue.text: Order son to leave joint

indicators.note: the letter leaving means it is taken out of the word

parts.note: the wrist is a joint

explanation.surface: An instruction for a son to walk out of a pub or dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes S out of WRIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order.
